title: Signal-hunt: midday kv/quant probe scratchpad
content:
Quick context and goals:
- Looking for intermittent failure modes where cached KV state (warm cache) interacts badly with low-bit quantized model weights and produces divergence/hallucination on repeated prompt patterns.
- Hypothesis: certain prompt prefixes cause the compiled kernel path to choose a different attention kernel + KV packing that amplifies numeric noise at 3/4-bit quant levels.
- Short-term goal: reproduce reliably, collect minimal repro, and capture exact input tokens and cache warm steps.

Run notes (ordered rough timeline):
- 2026-03-18 09:12: run signal-18-A (rw-slim-3b, 4-bit nf4, batch=8, seq=1024)
  - config: quant=4bit-nf4, compilation: kernel-set v2.14, kv-cache enabled, prefix-cache warmup=6 requests
  - observation: 4/32 runs had an unexpected token repetition after 2nd generation step (pattern: repeated filler phrase). p50 token latency ~38ms, p95 ~92ms.
- 2026-03-18 10:05: run signal-18-B (same prompts) but with cache-warm=0 (cold)
  - observation: no repeats, outputs aligned with baseline fp16 runs. Suggests cache interplay.
- 2026-03-18 11:20: run signal-18-C (3-bit experimental quant, batch=4)
  - observation: higher variance, (~12% of runs show semantic drift), but not identical failure mode to 4-bit. Latency slightly lower but instability higher.

Minimal repro candidate:
- Prompt prefix used for failures (shortened):
  - 'Task: extract the key entities from the text and summarize in one sentence. Do not hallucinate new facts.'
- Input text pattern: 2 paragraphs with repeated named entities and a trailing ambiguous referent (e.g., 'they' referencing two different people). Repeated short conjunctions seem to trigger the repeat.
- Repro steps: send prefix 6x to warm cache (identical), then send target prompt. If using 4-bit with kernel-set v2.14 and cache warm=6, reproduce ~30% of the time on gpu-a100-rt.

Prompt probes tried (short variations):
- probe-A: 'You are a precise extraction assistant. Extract names only.'
- probe-B: same but add 'If unsure, say "unknown".'
- probe-C: inject innocuous clarifier token 'Note: answer must be exact.'
- probe-D: change spacing/newline patterns between prefix and body
Observation: adding explicit "If unsure, say unknown" reduces hallucination but sometimes increases token repetition (tradeoff).

Quick hypotheses to test next:
- H1: numeric noise accumulates in KV when identical prefixes are cached repeatedly -> test by varying token-level perturbation of prefix (flip casing, small whitespace) and measure failure rate.
- H2: kernel selection boundary at seq-length chunking causes different attention tiling -> run with forced kernel v2.13 and v2.14 and compare.
- H3: beam/temperature interplay with 4-bit quant amplifies repeats -> try temperature=0.7 and 0.0.

Planned experiments (next 48h):
- E1 (small): run 100x of minimal repro on dedicated node gpu-a100-rt with quant 4bit vs fp16, cache-warm=6 and cache-warm=0. Collect token-level diffs and failure labels. (Owner: me)
- E2 (kernel): force kernel v2.13/v2.14 on same workload, capture kernel-selection logs and compiled kernel hashes. (Owner: Mikaela)
- E3 (prefix perturbation): automated script to generate 6 variants per prefix (case/whitespace/punct), run 50x each. (Owner: Noah)
- E4 (eval set): build 120-case eval from customer-like docs (finance / legal short snippets) to see domain sensitivity. (Owner: me, help: Noah)

Quick commands / helpers (notes to self):
- bench script: scripts/mini-bench/run_kv_probe.sh --model rw-slim-3b --quant nf4 --cache-warm 6 --batch 8 --seq 1024 --runs 100 --out results/signal-18-A.json
- collect kernel logs: /opt/runtime/bin/rt-kernel-log --since 2026-03-18T09:00 --to-file kernellogs/signal-18-kernels.log
- diff tokens: tools/token-diff.py results/..

Open questions / flags: 
- Is this user-visible for Hosted API customers with bursty prefix traffic? Could be, need quick detection rule in Console (per-route repeating token anomaly).
- Should we roll back kernel-set change if repro rate > 15% on committed dedicated nodes? Ops implications.
- Is there a correlation with particular batch sizes (8 vs 16) beyond simple throughput? initial signal suggests batch 8 more noisy in this workload.

Hands-on TODO (immediate):
- [ ] kick E1 on dedicated node (me)
- [ ] ask Mikaela for kernel selection trace capture and upload path (Mikaela)
- [ ] script prefix perturbation generator (Noah)
- [ ] add quick alert in Console: token-repeat-rate > 5% in last 1h for route X (quick draft)

Random thoughts / ephemeral notes:
- Might be useful to add a short random-token 'jitter' in prefix-caching mechanism to avoid exact identical cache keys across noisy clients (but must be opt-in).
- Could also try soft-KV expiration by request-time to reduce long-lived numeric accumulation.

End-of-day capture: 2026-03-18 18:45. Will update after E1 finishes (~3h).
